evidence.name: TextLineWrappingAndRendering

function_ir.summary: Renders a text line with word wrap onto an output context. When the special color marker 16909060 is passed as the color parameter, maps it to a render color mask via IDToColorMaskMapper. While the remaining text is at least 80 characters, copies 79-character segments, cuts each at the last space boundary after position 40 (or at 79 when no space found), and renders the segment via UtilityFunction_b9c0. Finally renders the remaining text. Skips rendering when the width/size parameter exceeds the global bound dword_7D02E4. Part of the UI/text rendering subsystem.

operations.description: Return the default value (dword_7D02E4) without rendering when the width/size parameter a3 exceeds the global bound dword_7D02E4.
When the color parameter a4 equals the special marker 16909060, map it to a render color mask via IDToColorMaskMapper(a3).

While the remaining text (a2 + offset) is at least 80 chars: copy a 79-char segment into the local buffer via sub_587DD0, null-terminate it, and scan backwards from position 78 to 40 for a space (0x20) break.
Choose the wrap point length: last space index + 1 when a space was found after position 40, otherwise the full 79-char segment.

Truncate the segment at the wrap point and render it via UtilityFunction_b9c0 with the output context (*this), color, fixed parameter 1084227584 and width parameter a3; advance the consumed text offset.
Render the remaining (final) text segment via UtilityFunction_b9c0 with the output context (*this).
Return the result of the final segment render (or the default guard value when rendering was skipped).

clean_pseudocode: return UtilityFunction_b9c0(*this, a2 + off, a4, 1084227584, a3);
unresolved: Global dword_59F07C is listed by the fact store but does not appear in the recovered source for this function; its role here is unconfirmed.
Meaning of the fixed render parameter 1084227584 is unconfirmed.
Exact meaning of the width/size parameter a3 and the bound dword_7D02E4 is unconfirmed.
